guides.wedding-checklist-generator.title: Wedding Planning Checklist: A 12-Month Timeline
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.desc: A month-by-month wedding planning checklist with the tasks that actually gate the next ones, plus what changes for UK and destination weddings.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.lead: Most checklists fail because they list 200 tasks as equals. The useful version is the dependency order: the bookings that must happen before anything else can be confirmed.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.f1v: Set a budget ceiling and a guest-count range before contacting venues
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.f2v: Venue, date, officiant and any visa or travel blocks
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.f3v: Save-the-dates, attire, photographer, catering and music
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.f4v: Final headcount, seating, timeline, vows and payments
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.s1: Work backwards from the date, not forwards from today. A venue determines the catering rules, the catering rules determine the meal count, and the meal count determines the seating chart. Changing the venue after invites are out breaks every downstream item, which is why it sits at the top.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.s2: In the US the engagement is often long and the registry opens early; in the UK it is common to send formal invitations six to eight weeks out and to skip the registry entirely. Destination weddings need a second, earlier track for travel documents, group room blocks and local marriage-licence residence requirements, which can be 3 to 30 days depending on the country.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.s3: The two mistakes that cost money are booking vendors before the guest-count range is fixed, and treating RSVPs as a single deadline. Add a buffer of two weeks between your reply-by date and the caterer's final headcount date, otherwise you will pay for no-shows and still chase late replies.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.q1: How far in advance should we start?
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.a1: Twelve to eighteen months for a Saturday in peak season at a popular venue. Six to nine months is realistic for a weekday, off-season or backyard wedding.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.q2: What goes on a wedding checklist?
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.a2: Budget, guest range, venue, officiant, legal paperwork, catering, attire, photography, music, stationery, transport, accommodation, timeline, payments and post-wedding thank-yous.
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.q3: Do we need a separate day-of timeline?
guides.wedding-checklist-generator.a3: Yes. A planning checklist covers months; the day-of timeline covers minutes, with vendor arrival windows, buffer time and a named point of contact for each handoff.
